paragraphs.text: Chapter 1. Going nowhere.
Haminda looked at her watch and then at the traffic outside. The airport was 10km away,
and it was already 5.15pm.
Isn't there a quicker way to get to the airport? My plane leaves in less than two hours.
She asked the taxi driver.
Are you going home for Christmas?
He smiled. The taxi was full of decorations. There was green tinsel on the steering wheel,
and mistletoe under the mirror.
Yes! said Haminda. But there was no Christmas spirit in her voice.
Haminda looked out of the window, trying not to cry. She remembered the phone call from
her mum earlier that day. She missed her parents so much. Their argument four years ago
seemed stupid now. Thirty minutes later they arrived at Galway Airport.
How much is it? She asked.
15 euros for you, sweetheart.
Said the taxi driver with a smile. Haminda gave him a 20 euro note and got quickly out
of the taxi.
Don't forget your change.
shouted the taxi driver with a 5 euro note in his hand. But Haminda was already inside the
airport terminal. There were a lot of people, and Haminda pushed through the crowd to look
at the screens for her flight.
Cancelled. Stay calm and read it again. Slowly. You've read it wrong. That's all.
She thought. Flight. Z-X-Y-247. Destination. London's
danced it. Cancelled.
All flights from Galway were cancelled because of bad weather. I'm sorry, but tomorrow's
flight to London is fully booked. Christmas is a busy time of year. Said the man at the
airport. What about another airport? Dublin perhaps.
Sorry. You don't understand. Said Haminda.
I have to get to London as soon as possible. My dad's ill.
I really am very sorry. The man said sympathetically. You could hire a car. It's a long journey,
but if you need to get there quickly, as Haminda ran towards car hire, she saw that there were
only two women waiting, and she started to feel hopeful.
I'm sorry, but this is the last car. She heard the assistant say.
But I was here first. Shouted a tall, blonde woman.
Only because you pushed in front of me. I'm getting married in three days. I have to get
to London. Shouted an Irish girl in her late twenties.
And I've got a very important audition. Said the blonde woman.
Excuse me. Interrupted, Haminda. Did you say that there's only one car? Yes, and it's mine.
Said the blonde, arrogantly. No, it's not. The argument continued. Haminda wanted to cry.
But then she had an idea. If you two are going to London, we can share the car. What do you think?
We can share the driving and the cost. The two women looked at her in silence.
They probably think I'm mad. Thought, Haminda. But that didn't worry her.
The only thing that worried her was getting to London to see her family.
Well, if you want to get to your audition. Haminda said to the blonde.
And if you want to get married. She said to the other woman.
Well, you've got no choice. Haminda was speaking angrily. And after a moment, the two women reluctantly agreed.
Mr. O'Flahity will be pleased. Thought Chrissy, the car hire assistant, as she showed the women their car.
Chrissy! Chrissy! A man shouted, running towards them. It was very cold, but he was sweating.
And his face was red and angry. Oh, that's my boss. Merry Christmas!
She smiled and closed the door. Stop them, Chrissy!
What? It's okay, Mr. O'Flahity. They've paid?
She smiled, waving at the car as it left. That car was reserved, you stupid girl.
He shouted. Chrissy's face turned red. She didn't see the three businessmen as she ran into the airport crying.
Where is my car, Mr. O'Flahity? Asked one. His voice was calm, but his grey eyes were dangerous.
Colin O'Flahity turned around nervously to talk to the three men. And he knew that he was in trouble. Big trouble.
